column1: skm2-c1-ni-saishite|Formal occasion|入学に際して、必要な書類を提出してください。|Please submit the required documents on entering the school.|Nに際して marks a formal/significant occasion; it is not a general replacement for every とき.

skm2-c1-ni-saishite|Beginning an undertaking|新しい事業を始めるにあたって、専門家に相談しました。|Before embarking on a new business, I consulted a specialist.|V dictionary + にあたって frames preparation for an undertaking. It is common with forward-looking occasions.

skm2-c1-ka-to-omou-to|Rapid change|空が暗くなったかと思うと、激しい雨が降り始めました。|The sky had barely darkened when heavy rain began.|The speaker observes a rapid transition, rather than stating a planned action triggered by a condition.

skm2-c1-ka-to-omou-to|Contrasting behavior|子供は泣いたかと思ったら、もう笑っていました。|The child had barely started crying before they were laughing again.|The change can be a striking contrast in behavior; the expression need not report a literal intervening thought.
skm2-c1-kanai-ka-no-uchini|Almost no time gap|ベルが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、学生たちが立ち上がりました。|The students stood up almost before the bell had rung.|The repeated verb frames the event at the boundary of completion.
skm2-c1-kanai-ka-no-uchini|Instant onset after arrival|家に着くか着かないかのうちに、雨が降り出しました。|It began raining just as I was arriving home.|This is an immediate temporal sequence, not a deliberate future request.

skm2-c1-tatan-ni|Unexpected immediate reaction|立ち上がったとたん、めまいがしました。|The moment I stood up, I felt dizzy.|Vたとたん links an immediate occurrence that was not presented as the speaker's planned next action.
skm2-c1-tatan-ni|Sudden change at a trigger|窓を開けたとたん、強い風が入ってきました。|The instant I opened the window, a strong wind blew in.|The first action is completed at the point the second event occurs.
added-n2-1-69|Formal noun phrase|お申し込みの際に、身分証明書をご提示ください。|Please present identification when applying.|Nの際に is formal wording for an occasion and can introduce an instruction.
added-n2-1-69|Past-form occasion|京都を訪れた際に、先生にお会いしました。|When I visited Kyoto, I met my teacher.|Vた際に describes a past occasion; 際に is not limited to future beginnings.
skm2-c2-saichuu-da|Interruption during an activity|会議をしている最中に、停電しました。|There was a power cut right in the middle of the meeting.|An interruption is common after 最中に; the ongoing activity uses ている.
skm2-c2-saichuu-da|State without an interruption|今は準備の最中です。|We are in the middle of preparations now.|Nの最中だ simply states an ongoing phase; it does not require an unexpected bad event.

skm2-c2-ippou-da-bakari-da|Unfavorable trend|修理をしないので、状態は悪くなるばかりです。|Because it is not being repaired, its condition keeps getting worse.|ばかりだ presents a one-direction trend, often evaluated negatively.

skm2-c2-ippou-da-bakari-da|Favorable or neutral trend|利用者は増える一方です。|The number of users keeps increasing.|一方だ does not itself state whether the growth is good or bad, or whether its rate is accelerating.
skm2-c2-tsutsu-aru|Change underway|町の景色は少しずつ変わりつつあります。|The townscape is gradually changing.|V-stem + つつある presents a process of change underway, often in formal writing.
skm2-c2-tsutsu-aru|Recovery underway|景気は回復しつつあります。|The economy is in the process of recovering.|The construction highlights transition; it is not the ordinary way to say a person is eating right now.
added-n2-2-70|Act before a state changes|暗くならないうちに、帰りましょう。|Let's go home before it gets dark.|ないうちに sets a limited opportunity before the state changes.
added-n2-2-70|Imminent event|長い冬が終わろうとしています。|The long winter is about to end.|Volitional + としている can describe an event on the verge of occurring, without a human agent intending it.

added-n2-2-71|Simultaneous action|資料を確認しつつ、説明を聞きました。|I listened to the explanation while checking the documents.|V-stemつつ can link simultaneous activities by the same actor, in a relatively formal style.
added-n2-2-71|Concession|悪いと知りつつも、約束を破ってしまいました。|Although I knew it was wrong, I broke the promise.|つつも expresses a conflict between awareness and action, not simultaneity alone.

skm2-c3-te-hajimete|New understanding after experience|一人で暮らしてはじめて、家事の大変さが分かりました。|Only after living alone did I understand how hard housework is.|The experience enables a realization not previously attained.

skm2-c3-te-hajimete|Necessary first step|実際に使ってはじめて、この道具の便利さが分かります。|Only by actually using it can you appreciate how useful this tool is.|The first action is necessary for the later understanding; this is not simply two events in sequence.
skm2-c3-ue-de|After deliberate prerequisite|内容をよく確認した上で、署名してください。|Please sign after checking the contents carefully.|Vた上で treats the completed action as a prerequisite for the next step.

skm2-c3-ue-de|In the course of doing|仕事を選ぶ上で、何を大切にしていますか。|What do you consider important when choosing a job?|V dictionary上で identifies the activity or standpoint within which a consideration matters; it does not mean after choosing.
added-n2-3-72|Planned action immediately after a trigger|日程が決まり次第、ご連絡します。|I will contact you as soon as the schedule is decided.|V-stem次第 introduces the future trigger for a planned response.

added-n2-3-72|Request tied to completion|準備ができ次第、出発してください。|Please leave as soon as the preparations are complete.|The final clause can be a request; distinguish temporal 次第 from N次第 meaning depending on.
added-n2-3-73|Continuing since an event|日本へ来て以来、毎日日記を書いています。|I have kept a diary every day since coming to Japan.|て以来 presents continuity over the period after the starting event.

added-n2-3-73|Sustained state since a major change|引っ越してこのかた、前の友達には会っていません。|Since moving, I have not seen my old friends.|てこのかた is a relatively formal expression emphasizing the period since the event.

added-n2-3-74|Prerequisite for a decision|実物を見てからでないと、買うかどうか決められません。|I cannot decide whether to buy it until I see the actual item.|The consequence is negative in meaning before the prerequisite is satisfied.

added-n2-3-74|Negative evaluation without ない|許可をもらってからでなければ、使用は無理です。|Using it is impossible until permission has been obtained.|無理 provides the negative meaning; the grammar does not require a literal ない ending.

skm2-c4-wo-hajime|Representative example in a wider group|校長先生をはじめ、多くの先生が出席しました。|Many teachers attended, including the principal.|The principal is a prominent representative, not necessarily the first person in chronological order.
skm2-c4-wo-hajime|Modifying a noun group|京都をはじめとする古い町を訪ねました。|I visited old towns including Kyoto.|をはじめとする modifies the following noun phrase.
skm2-c4-kara-shite|An initial feature as evidence|この店は入口からして、とても豪華です。|Even the entrance to this shop is very luxurious.|からして singles out an initial/basic feature suggesting what the whole is like.

skm2-c4-kara-shite|Judging from a clue|話し方からして、かなり緊張しているようです。|Judging from the way they speak, they seem quite nervous.|The feature is used as a basis for inference; do not translate it as a starting time.
skm2-c4-ni-watatte|Extended time|工事は三か月にわたって続きました。|The construction continued over three months.|にわたって emphasizes the extent of the period, rather than naming a starting point.
skm2-c4-ni-watatte|Geographical scope|大雨の被害は県全体にわたっています。|The damage from heavy rain extends across the whole prefecture.|The scope can be spatial rather than temporal.
added-n2-4-75|Throughout a period|この地域は一年を通じて温暖です。|This region is mild throughout the year.|を通じて describes a condition spanning a whole period.
added-n2-4-75|An intermediary or medium|友人を通して、その仕事を知りました。|I learned about the job through a friend.|を通して names an intermediary, not the duration of the event.
added-n2-4-76|Maximum possible effort|できる限り、手伝います。|I will help as much as I can.|限り expresses the maximum extent within the speaker's ability.
added-n2-4-76|As much as possible|今日は食べられるだけ食べてください。|Please eat as much as you can today.|Potential verb + だけ sets the possible extent. It is not merely only eat rather than drink.
skm2-c4-kagiri-dewa|Limited knowledge|私が知っている限りでは、その店は日曜も開いています。|As far as I know, that shop is open on Sundays too.|The statement is limited to the speaker's information, not guaranteed beyond it.

skm2-c4-kagiri-dewa|Limited investigation|調べた限りでは、問題は見つかりませんでした。|As far as my investigation went, no problem was found.|The phrase qualifies the evidence base; it does not prove that no problem exists anywhere.
added-n2-5-77|Restriction to a group|会員に限り、入場料が無料です。|Admission is free for members only.|に限り restricts eligibility; it does not mean members are the best choice.
added-n2-5-77|An unfortunate particular occasion|急いでいる日に限って、電車が遅れます。|The train is delayed on the very days when I am in a hurry.|に限って singles out an inconvenient occasion, often with frustration.

added-n2-5-77|Trust in a particular person|あの人に限って、約束を忘れるはずがありません。|That person of all people surely would not forget a promise.|に限って identifies someone the speaker trusts to be an exception; it is different from an eligibility restriction.

added-n2-5-78|Condition that remains true|ここに住んでいる限りは、町の規則を守らなければなりません。|As long as you live here, you must follow the town's rules.|限りは states the continuing condition under which the conclusion holds.

added-n2-5-78|Boundary of available information|私が聞いた限りでは、計画に変更はありません。|As far as I have heard, there is no change to the plan.|限りでは restricts the information supporting the claim, not the period during which a duty holds.

skm2-c5-nomi-narazu|Formal addition|この研究は国内のみならず、海外でも注目されています。|This research is attracting attention not only domestically but overseas too.|のみならず is a formal additive expression; も commonly marks the added scope.

skm2-c5-nomi-narazu|More than one quality|彼は知識が豊富であるのみならず、説明も上手です。|He is not only knowledgeable but also good at explaining.|A formal predicate can precede のみならず; the second clause adds another quality.
skm2-c5-bakari-ka|An added, stronger fact|この店は安いばかりか、配達まで無料です。|This shop is not only cheap; even delivery is free.|ばかりか adds a further point, often stronger or more surprising than the first.
skm2-c5-bakari-ka|Unexpected negative addition|彼は謝らないばかりか、私を責めました。|He not only failed to apologize; he blamed me.|The added point can intensify an unfavorable evaluation.
added-n2-6-79|Not restricted to one group|この講座は学生に限らず、社会人も参加できます。|This course is open not only to students but also to working adults.|に限らず expands the scope beyond the first group.
added-n2-6-79|The first point is taken for granted|日本語はもとより、英語でも説明できます。|They can explain in English as well as, of course, Japanese.|はもとより treats the first case as already expected and adds another.

added-n2-6-79|Another circumstance in addition|この部屋は広い上に、駅にも近いです。|This room is spacious and is also near the station.|上に adds another circumstance supporting the same overall evaluation; it is not temporal 上で.

skm2-c7-wo-megutte|Debate around an issue|新しい道路の建設をめぐって、住民の意見が分かれています。|Residents are divided over construction of the new road.|をめぐって frames the issue around which debate or differing positions develop.
skm2-c7-wo-megutte|Modify a noun|土地の利用をめぐる話し合いが続いています。|Discussions over land use are continuing.|をめぐる modifies the following noun; the pattern is not restricted to angry arguments.

skm2-c7-ni-kotaete|Respond to a request|利用者の要望にこたえて、営業時間を延ばしました。|In response to users' requests, we extended the opening hours.|にこたえて means acting to meet a request or expectation, not merely answering a question verbally.
skm2-c7-ni-kotaete|Meet expectations|両親の期待にこたえられるよう、努力しています。|I am working hard so that I can live up to my parents' expectations.|The potential form describes being able to meet the expectation.

skm2-c13-ni-kakete-wa|Strength in a field|料理にかけては、姉のほうが得意です。|When it comes to cooking, my older sister is better at it.|にかけては highlights a field of strength; it does not by itself mean best in the world.

skm2-c13-ni-kakete-wa|Confident assessment|正確さにかけては、この方法が優れています。|In terms of accuracy, this method is superior.|The following predicate evaluates a particular strength rather than just naming a neutral topic.
skm2-c6-ni-kansuru|Topic of a discussion|環境問題に関して、意見を交換しました。|We exchanged opinions concerning environmental issues.|に関して is a relatively formal topic marker.
skm2-c6-ni-kansuru|Modify a noun|奨学金に関する資料を読みました。|I read materials concerning scholarships.|に関する is the noun-modifying form; に関して is not substituted directly before 資料.
added-n2-7-80|Target of an attitude|政府に対して、不満を持つ人が増えています。|More people are dissatisfied with the government.|に対して identifies the target of dissatisfaction.
added-n2-7-80|Noun modification|学生に対する説明が不足していました。|The explanation given to students was insufficient.|に対する modifies 説明; preserve the target relationship when changing the grammatical form.
skm2-c8-ni-motozuite|Grounds for a decision|調査の結果に基づいて、計画を見直しました。|We revised the plan based on the survey results.|に基づいて identifies the grounds for the revision.

skm2-c8-ni-motozuite|Source material|この映画は実際の出来事をもとに作られました。|This film was made based on actual events.|をもとに identifies source material; it does not guarantee that every detail is reproduced literally.
skm2-c8-ni-sotte|Physical path|川に沿って、細い道が続いています。|A narrow road runs along the river.|沿う can describe following a physical line, not just an abstract policy.
skm2-c8-ni-sotte|Guiding plan|計画に沿って、作業を進めます。|We will proceed with the work according to the plan.|に沿って presents the plan as a guiding line for the work.
added-n2-8-81|Guidance or environment|有名な先生のもとで、研究を続けました。|I continued my research under a well-known teacher.|のもとで identifies the guidance or environment under which an activity occurs.
added-n2-8-81|Shared principle or condition|安全第一という方針のもとに、作業を進めます。|We will proceed under a policy of safety first.|のもとに identifies the principle or condition governing the activity.

added-n2-8-82|Intended audience|これは初心者向けの教科書です。|This is a textbook intended for beginners.|向け describes the target audience for which something is designed, not a guarantee that every beginner finds it suitable.
added-n2-8-82|Action aimed at an audience|外国人向けに、やさしい日本語で案内を書きました。|I wrote the information in simple Japanese for foreign readers.|向けに modifies the action; 向けの modifies a noun.
skm2-c9-ni-tsurete|Gradual linked change|年を取るにつれて、考え方が変わりました。|My way of thinking changed as I grew older.|につれて links a progression with another developing change.

skm2-c9-ni-tsurete|Progress in one process|山を登るにしたがって、空気が冷たくなりました。|The air became colder as we climbed the mountain.|にしたがって links the progressing climb to the changing temperature; it does not assert an exact mathematical rate.
skm2-c9-ni-oujite|Adapt to a condition|経験に応じて、仕事を分担します。|We will assign work according to experience.|に応じて describes an adjustment matched to the relevant condition.
skm2-c9-ni-oujite|Noun modification|能力に応じた指導が必要です。|Instruction suited to ability is necessary.|に応じた modifies the following noun and presents suitability, not merely a simultaneous change.

added-n2-9-83|Accompanying development|人口の増加に伴って、交通量も増えています。|Traffic is also increasing along with population growth.|に伴って links accompanying developments; it is common in relatively formal explanations.
added-n2-9-83|Change alongside change|年齢とともに、体力は変わります。|Physical strength changes with age.|とともに can link developments; in other contexts it means together with, so identify the relevant use.
added-n2-9-84|Depends on a factor|成功するかどうかは、準備次第です。|Whether it succeeds depends on the preparation.|N次第だ makes the outcome dependent on a factor; it is different from V-stem次第 meaning as soon as.
added-n2-9-84|Recurring trigger for a feeling|この写真を見るにつけて、故郷を思い出します。|Whenever I see this photograph, I remember my hometown.|につけて presents an occasion that repeatedly calls up a thought or feeling.

added-n2-10-85|An unsettled or varied list|引っ越しの準備やら仕事やらで、忙しいです。|I am busy with moving preparations, work, and all sorts of things.|やら lists examples, often suggesting a mixed or burdensome assortment rather than an exhaustive list.

added-n2-10-85|Searching for a description|驚いたというか、あきれたというか、言葉が出ませんでした。|I was surprised—or perhaps exasperated—and could not find words.|というか offers/revises descriptions as the speaker searches for fitting wording.
added-n2-10-86|Either of two alternatives|電車にしてもバスにしても、一時間はかかります。|Whether by train or bus, it takes at least an hour.|にしても…にしても makes a statement applying to either named case.
added-n2-10-86|Another alternative frame|行くにしろ行かないにしろ、早く連絡してください。|Whether you go or not, please let me know soon.|にしろ presents alternatives without changing the request.

added-n2-10-86|Representative examples before a noun|京都や奈良といった町は、観光客に人気があります。|Cities such as Kyoto and Nara are popular with tourists.|といった introduces representative examples of the following category.
skm2-c11-ni-kakawarazu|Independent of a variable|経験の有無にかかわらず、応募できます。|You can apply regardless of whether you have experience.|にかかわらず says the result does not depend on that variable.
skm2-c11-ni-kakawarazu|Positive and negative alternatives|参加するしないにかかわらず、返信してください。|Please reply regardless of whether you will participate.|The two verb forms explicitly give the alternative cases.

skm2-c11-ha-tomo-kaku|Set one evaluation aside|値段はともかく、品質はとてもいいです。|Leaving the price aside, the quality is very good.|The speaker postpones judging one aspect to focus on another; it need not mean the price is bad.

skm2-c11-ha-tomo-kaku|Whether a proposition is true|成功するかどうかはともかく、まず試してみましょう。|Whether it will succeed or not aside, let's try it first.|The set-aside material can be an embedded question, not just a single noun.
skm2-c11-ha-sateoki|Return to the priority|冗談はさておき、本題に入りましょう。|Joking aside, let's get to the main topic.|はさておき explicitly puts one topic aside to proceed with another.
skm2-c11-ha-sateoki|Postpone one issue|詳しい日程はさておき、まず場所を決めましょう。|Leaving the detailed schedule for now, let's first decide the venue.|The postponed issue is not necessarily unimportant or false.
added-n2-11-87|No restriction by category|年齢を問わず、誰でも参加できます。|Anyone can participate regardless of age.|を問わず removes a categorical restriction; it is common in notices.

added-n2-11-87|Disregarding a concern|周囲の目もかまわず、大声で泣いてしまいました。|I cried loudly without caring about people watching.|もかまわず describes disregarding something that might normally restrain the action, not equal eligibility across categories.
skm2-c12-dokoroka|Contrary to the proposed situation|休むどころか、昨日より忙しくなりました。|Far from resting, I became busier than yesterday.|どころか overturns the expected description with a contrasting reality.

skm2-c12-dokoroka|Even a lower threshold is not met|漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めません。|I cannot even read hiragana, let alone kanji.|The construction can deny even a lesser expectation; it is not restricted to a worse physical outcome.
added-n2-12-88|Strong rejection of possibility|一日でこの本を全部覚えられるわけがありません。|There is no way I can memorize this whole book in one day.|わけがない rejects a possibility from the speaker's reasoning.
added-n2-12-88|Emotional rejection|もう二度とあんな店に行くものか。|There is no way I am ever going to that shop again.|ものか expresses a forceful negative intention or rejection, not an ordinary information question.
added-n2-12-88|Reject a simplistic generalization|長く勉強すればいいというものではありません。|Studying longer is not necessarily all that matters.|というものではない rejects the claim as an adequate general rule.

added-n2-13-89|Define a term|敬語とは、相手との関係を考えて使う表現です。|Honorific language is language used with regard to one's relationship with others.|とは can introduce a definition; it is not always a surprised exclamation.
added-n2-13-89|Pick up an associated topic|京都といえば、古いお寺を思い出します。|Speaking of Kyoto, I think of old temples.|といえば takes a topic and introduces something associated with it.
added-n2-13-89|A topic changes behavior|仕事のこととなると、彼は急に真剣になります。|When it comes to work, he suddenly becomes serious.|のこととなると highlights a topic/situation that prompts a characteristic reaction.
added-n2-13-90|Strong impression|あの景色の美しさといったら、言葉では表せません。|The beauty of that scenery was beyond words.|といったら emphasizes an impressive degree and often invites an emotional evaluation.
added-n2-13-90|Negative impression|朝の電車の混雑といったら、本当に大変です。|The crowding on the morning train is really something awful.|The emphasized impression can be unfavorable; といったら is not inherently praise.

skm2-c19-monono|Admit a fact, contrast the result|本は買ったものの、まだ読んでいません。|Although I bought the book, I have not read it yet.|ものの acknowledges the first fact while introducing a situation that fails to meet the expectation it creates.

skm2-c19-monono|Qualify a broad description|春とはいうものの、まだ寒い日が続いています。|Although it is spring, cold days are still continuing.|とはいうものの concedes the description, then qualifies what might be inferred from it.
added-n2-14-91|Despite an established circumstance|雨にもかかわらず、多くの人が集まりました。|Despite the rain, many people gathered.|にもかかわらず marks concession; distinguish にかかわらず, which says the variable does not matter.

added-n2-14-91|Clause before the concession|十分準備したにもかかわらず、失敗しました。|Although I prepared thoroughly, I failed.|A plain clause can precede にもかかわらず; the result contradicts the expectation from that preparation.

added-n2-14-92|Concession with ながらも|狭いながらも、我が家は温かくて居心地がいい。|Although it is small, our home is warm and cozy.|Concessive ながらも attaches to an adjective or noun to concede a modest condition while asserting a positive reality.

added-n2-14-92|Qualify the meaning of a statement|料理ができるといっても、簡単な物だけです。|Although I say I can cook, I can only make simple things.|といっても limits what the listener should infer from the preceding description.

added-n2-14-92|Reject an inference from a reason|安いからといって、必要のない物を買うべきではありません。|You should not buy things you do not need just because they are cheap.|からといって commonly appears with a conclusion denying that the reason alone justifies an inference or action.

skm2-c15-mono-nara|Difficult-to-realize wish|昔に戻れるものなら、もう一度やり直したいです。|If I could go back to the past, I would like to start over.|Potential + ものなら assumes a possibility regarded as difficult or impossible; the wish follows from that assumption.

skm2-c15-mono-nara|A challenging hypothetical possibility|一人でできるものなら、やってみてください。|If you really can do it alone, try it.|The construction can challenge a claimed ability; it is not restricted to desperate longing.
skm2-c15-nai-koto-niwa|Information prerequisite|実際に見ないことには、判断できません。|I cannot judge it unless I actually see it.|ないことには sets a necessary condition before a negative conclusion.
skm2-c15-nai-koto-niwa|State as prerequisite|元気でないことには、仕事も楽しめません。|Unless I am well, I cannot enjoy work either.|A な-adjective uses でないことには; the prerequisite need not be an action.

skm2-c15-wo-nuki-ni-shite-wa|Necessary contributor|仲間の協力を抜きにしては、この成功はあり得ませんでした。|This success would not have been possible without my colleagues' cooperation.|The は construction identifies something indispensable to the outcome.

skm2-c15-wo-nuki-ni-shite-wa|Necessary consideration|費用の問題を抜きにしては、計画を立てられません。|We cannot make a plan without considering the issue of cost.|The indispensable element can be a consideration, not a person being thanked.
added-n2-15-93|Assumed situation|もし一週間休めるとしたら、何をしたいですか。|If you could take a week off, what would you like to do?|としたら explicitly sets up an assumption; it does not claim the time off is available.
added-n2-15-93|Inference from an assumed premise|彼が来ないとすると、会議を延期する必要があります。|If he is not coming, we need to postpone the meeting.|とすると draws a consequence from taking the premise as true.
added-n2-15-93|Concession even under an assumption|参加できるとしても、一時間だけです。|Even if I can participate, it will only be for an hour.|としても keeps a qualification in place even if the assumption holds.

added-n2-15-94|Feared consequence of an action|この秘密を話そうものなら、大変なことになります。|If someone were to reveal this secret, there would be serious trouble.|Volitional + ものなら imagines an action with a feared or severe consequence; it differs from potential + ものなら.

added-n2-15-94|An exaggerated warning|その犬に近づこうものなら、大声でほえられますよ。|If you so much as try to approach that dog, it will bark loudly at you.|The speaker emphasizes the undesirable consequence of even attempting the action.
skm2-c16-amari-excess|Excessive feeling|心配のあまり、何度も電話をかけました。|I was so worried that I called repeatedly.|Nのあまり presents excessive worry as the cause of the action.
skm2-c16-amari-excess|Excessive action, not only emotion|働きすぎたあまり、体を壊してしまいました。|I worked so excessively that I damaged my health.|The cause can be an excessive action, not only a psychological state.
skm2-c16-amari-excess|Fronted degree phrase|あまりの暑さに、外へ出るのをやめました。|Because of the extreme heat, I decided not to go outside.|あまりのNに places the degree phrase before the noun describing the cause.
added-n2-16-95|Cause in a formal account|事故によって、道路が閉鎖されました。|The road was closed because of an accident.|によって identifies the cause; its other uses include means and passive agency.

added-n2-16-95|Personal explanation or excuse|道が混んでいたものですから、遅くなりました。|I am late because the roads were congested.|ものだから/ものですから often explains a personal circumstance, sometimes as an excuse; tone matters.
added-n2-16-95|Notice-style reason|工事中につき、立ち入り禁止です。|No entry due to construction work.|Nにつき is concise formal notice language for a reason; it is not ordinary casual conversation.

added-n2-16-96|Positive attribution|先生の指導のおかげで、自信がつきました。|Thanks to my teacher's guidance, I gained confidence.|おかげ attributes a result favorably; it is not restricted to a material gift or one particular benefactor.
added-n2-16-96|Unfavorable attribution|寝不足のせいで、集中できません。|I cannot concentrate because of lack of sleep.|せい attributes an unwanted effect; the cause need not be another person to blame.
added-n2-16-96|Degree leading to a result|驚きのあまり、声が出ませんでした。|I was so surprised that I could not speak.|あまり focuses on excessive degree, rather than simple favorable/unfavorable attribution.

skm2-c18-dakeni|Expectation strengthened by a reason|長く練習しただけに、自信がありました。|Precisely because I had practiced for a long time, I felt confident.|だけに presents the reason as making the conclusion particularly strong or understandable.

skm2-c18-dakeni|Disappointment strengthened by expectation|期待していただけに、結果を見てがっかりしました。|Because I had high expectations, I was especially disappointed by the result.|The reason can intensify a reaction contrary to the hoped-for outcome.

added-n2-17-97|One available reason for a proposal|雨もやんだことだし、散歩に行きましょう。|Now that the rain has stopped, among other things, let's go for a walk.|ことだし offers a relevant reason for proceeding, often implying other supporting circumstances.

added-n2-17-97|Inference from a known person's character|慎重な田中さんのことだから、もう確認したでしょう。|Knowing how careful Tanaka is, they have probably checked already.|Nのことだから bases an expectation on the person's familiar character or habits.
added-n2-17-98|One regretted cause|少し油断したばかりに、大切な物をなくしました。|Just because I let my guard down a little, I lost something important.|ばかりに singles out a cause with regret about the outcome.
added-n2-17-98|Commitment from a premise|引き受けたからには、最後までやります。|Now that I have accepted it, I will see it through.|からには treats the premise as grounds for resolve or an appropriate obligation.
added-n2-17-98|Duty following from a position|代表である以上は、責任を持つべきです。|As the representative, one should take responsibility.|以上は draws a normative consequence from the accepted position.

added-n2-17-98|Formal resolve|こうなった上は、計画を変えるしかありません。|Now that things have come to this, we have no choice but to change the plan.|上は is a formal way to present a settled premise for a decision; it differs from temporal 上で.
skm2-c22-kaneru|Formal refusal|そのご要望にはお応えしかねます。|We regret that we cannot meet that request.|かねる is a formal difficulty/refusal expression despite lacking a negative ending.
skm2-c22-kaneru|Difficulty accepting a position|その説明には納得しかねます。|I find that explanation difficult to accept.|The inability can be psychological/judgmental, not physical incapacity.
added-n2-18-99|Hard to accept or do|彼の話は信じがたいです。|His story is hard to believe.|V-stemがたい is common with psychological difficulty or strong judgments, not every ordinary physical difficulty.

added-n2-18-99|No available way|連絡先が分からないので、連絡しようがありません。|There is no way to contact them because I do not know their contact details.|ようがない means no means/way is available; しよう here is not the volitional form used for an invitation.

added-n2-18-99|Possible versus impossible|そんな間違いは誰にでも起こり得ます。絶対にないとは言い切れません。|Such a mistake can happen to anyone. We cannot say it will never happen.|V-stem得る expresses possibility. Dictionary 得る can be える or うる in this suffix use; 得ない is えない.

added-n2-18-100|Social/situational constraint|秘密なので、詳しく話すわけにはいきません。|Because it is confidential, I cannot explain it in detail.|わけにはいかない expresses a constraint on what is appropriate, not inability to form the words.

added-n2-18-100|Other circumstances leave no room|忙しくて、旅行どころではありません。|I am so busy that travel is out of the question.|どころではない says the circumstances leave no room for the activity; it is not a comparison meaning far from X, actually Y.

added-n2-19-101|Unexpected degree relative to a standard|この店は値段のわりに、量が多いです。|The portions at this restaurant are large for the price.|Nのわりに compares the actual degree with an expectation based on the price.

added-n2-19-101|Unexpected result given a specific description|初めて作ったにしては、よくできています。|For a first attempt at making it, it is well done.|にしては evaluates the result against the stated premise. It does not add の after a noun the way わりに does.

added-n2-19-102|Expected value proves justified|毎日練習しているだけのことはあります。演奏がとても上手です。|The daily practice shows: the performance is very good.|だけのことはある says the result is worthy of the effort/background described.

added-n2-19-102|Worth the cost|高いだけのことはあって、この靴はとても丈夫です。|These shoes are worth their high price: they are very durable.|The evaluation affirms an expected quality rather than marking a disappointing contrast.
added-n2-19-103|Role|親として、子供の意見をよく聞きたいです。|As a parent, I want to listen carefully to my child's views.|として states a capacity or role.
added-n2-19-103|Evaluating standpoint|私にとって、この経験は大きな財産です。|To me, this experience is a great asset.|にとって identifies the standpoint from which the value judgment is made.

added-n2-19-103|Imagine another person's position|子供にしたら、急な転校は不安でしょう。|From the child's point of view, a sudden change of school would be worrying.|にしたら asks us to consider a person's position and likely reaction.

skm2-c20-sue-ni-deliberation|Positive outcome after a process|何度も相談した末に、全員が納得する案を選びました。|After repeated discussions, we chose a proposal everyone accepted.|末に looks back over the process leading to the outcome; the result can be positive.

skm2-c20-sue-ni-deliberation|Unfavorable outcome|長い交渉の末に、契約は成立しませんでした。|After lengthy negotiations, no contract was concluded.|Nの末に also permits an unfavorable conclusion; it is not inherently a success formula.

skm2-c20-ageku-ni|Unwanted eventual result|長い時間待ったあげく、店に入れませんでした。|After waiting a long time, I still could not get into the restaurant.|あげく commonly presents a disappointing result after a troublesome process.
skm2-c20-ageku-ni|Noun before the pattern|何時間もの議論のあげく、結論は出ませんでした。|After hours of discussion, no conclusion was reached.|Nのあげく links the preceding process to the unwanted result.

added-n2-20-104|Action reveals a result|店に電話したところ、今日は休みだと分かりました。|When I called the shop, I found out it was closed today.|Vたところ reports the result discovered after trying an action; distinguish it from phase Vたところだ.

added-n2-20-104|Last event followed by no expected change|彼は出かけたきり、戻ってきません。|He went out and has not come back since.|Vたきり marks a last event after which the expected subsequent action has not occurred.
added-n2-20-104|Ended without doing it|忙しくて、友達に会わずじまいでした。|I was busy and ended up not seeing my friend.|ずじまい reports that the opportunity ended without the action being done, often with regret.
added-n2-21-105|Minimal example|名前くらいは覚えておいてください。|Please at least remember the name.|くらい presents a minimal expectation here, not an approximate quantity.
added-n2-21-105|Dismissive example|うわさなど気にしなくていいです。|You need not worry about things like rumors.|など can downplay the example; the tone can be dismissive depending on context.

added-n2-21-105|Going as far as a costly action|借金までして買うつもりはありません。|I do not intend to go so far as borrowing money to buy it.|Nまでして emphasizes the extent of the means taken; it often signals that the step is excessive.
added-n2-21-105|Verb te-form before まで|無理をしてまで、参加しなくてもいいです。|You do not have to push yourself just to participate.|Vてまで presents an extreme step taken to achieve another action.
added-n2-21-106|Not a single exception|一日として忘れたことはありません。|There has not been a single day when I forgot it.|A number expression + として + negative emphasizes the absence of even one exception.
added-n2-21-106|Even an unexpected case|子供でさえ、そのことを知っています。|Even children know that.|さえ includes an extreme or unexpected example; it is distinct from conditional さえ…ば.
added-n2-21-106|Resolve despite the cost|徹夜してでも、今日中に終わらせます。|I will finish it today even if I have to stay up all night.|てでも presents a means the speaker is willing to take to achieve the goal.

skm2-c21-ni-kimatte-iru|Confident inference|あんなに練習したのだから、うまくできるに決まっています。|After all that practice, I am sure they can do it well.|に決まっている expresses strong conviction; it does not establish objective certainty.
skm2-c21-ni-kimatte-iru|Noun predicate|そんな話は冗談に決まっています。|That story must be a joke.|A non-past noun attaches directly without だ in this construction.

skm2-c22-osore-ga-aru|Risk of an adverse event|大雨で、川の水があふれる恐れがあります。|There is a risk that the river will overflow because of heavy rain.|恐れがある is a relatively formal way to state an undesirable possibility.

skm2-c22-osore-ga-aru|Negative predicate as the risk|このままでは、締め切りに間に合わない恐れがあります。|At this rate, there is a risk we will not meet the deadline.|The feared event itself can be negative, expressed by Vない before 恐れがある.

skm2-c21-ni-chigai-nai|Inference from evidence|電気がついているので、誰かいるに違いありません。|The light is on, so someone must be there.|The speaker infers a conclusion from evidence; the evidence could still be misleading.
skm2-c21-ni-chigai-nai|Formal variant|この署名は本人のものに相違ありません。|This signature is undoubtedly the person's own.|に相違ない is a formal variant used for a confident assertion, not a different negative meaning.
skm2-c22-kane-nai|Possible unwanted consequence|そんな運転をすると、事故を起こしかねません。|Driving like that could cause an accident.|かねない has an unwanted possibility meaning despite its negative-looking ending.

skm2-c22-kane-nai|Less dramatic but unwanted result|説明が足りないと、誤解されかねません。|Without enough explanation, you could be misunderstood.|The unwanted outcome need not be a catastrophe; ordinary undesirable consequences are possible.
added-n2-22-107|Inference from signs|疲れているとみえて、彼はほとんど話しません。|He appears tired and hardly speaks.|とみえる presents an inference from signs; it is not direct proof of the internal state.

added-n2-22-107|Tentative rhetorical proposal|別の方法が必要なのではあるまいか。|Might a different method be needed?|ではあるまいか cautiously proposes a possibility; it is not simply a negative prediction that the method will not be needed.
skm2-c23-mono-da-essence|General observation|人の考えは変わるものです。|People's thinking changes over time.|ものだ presents a general observation; it does not claim a mathematical law without exceptions.

skm2-c23-mono-da-essence|Recollection of repeated experience|子供のころ、よく川で遊んだものです。|When I was a child, I used to play in the river.|Vたものだ recalls repeated past experience, often with reflection. It is not merely a report of one dated event.
skm2-c23-ni-koshita-koto-wa-nai|Prudent preference|準備は早いに越したことはありません。|It is best to prepare early.|The speaker endorses a preferable/prudent condition rather than guaranteeing it is always necessary.
skm2-c23-ni-koshita-koto-wa-nai|Action is preferable|念のため、確認するに越したことはありません。|To be on the safe side, it is best to check.|Dictionary verb + に越したことはない recommends the safer or preferable course.

added-n2-23-108|Evaluate as a fitting description|無断で人の物を使うのは、失礼というものです。|Using someone's things without permission is what one would call rude.|というものだ presents a description as a fitting or reasonable evaluation.
added-n2-23-108|Limit the significance|これは一つの例にすぎません。|This is merely one example.|にすぎない limits what is being claimed; it does not necessarily express uncertainty about its truth.
added-n2-23-109|Emphatic identification of a reason|成功したのは、みんなが協力したからにほかなりません。|The success was due to nothing other than everyone's cooperation.|からにほかならない emphasizes the essential reason.
added-n2-23-109|Lack of alternatives|電車がないので、歩くしかありません。|There is no train, so we have no choice but to walk.|V dictionaryしかない states that no alternative remains in the situation.
added-n2-23-109|Appropriate action|分からないことは、質問すべきです。|You should ask about what you do not understand.|べき expresses what the speaker considers appropriate, not physical necessity.
skm2-c24-koto-da|Practical advice|上達したければ、毎日少しずつ練習することです。|If you want to improve, you should practice a little every day.|Sentence-final ことだ gives advice about what to do; it may sound authoritative.

skm2-c24-koto-da|Direct negative advice|体を壊したくなければ、無理な残業はしないことです。|If you don't want to ruin your health, you shouldn't do unreasonable overtime.|V-ない + ことだ provides direct, firm advice on what action to avoid.
skm2-p2-mai|Negative intention|同じ失敗は繰り返すまいと思いました。|I resolved not to repeat the same mistake.|A first-person agent and intention context support the negative-will reading.
skm2-p2-mai|Negative conjecture|この時間では、もう誰も来るまい。|At this hour, probably nobody else will come.|まい is a formal negative conjecture here, not the speaker deciding not to come.
added-n2-24-110|Formal invitation to act together|もう一度、みんなで考えようではありませんか。|Let us all think about it once more.|Volitional + ではないか makes a formal appeal to joint action.
added-n2-24-110|No need to act|そんなに心配することはありません。|There is no need to worry so much.|Dictionary verb + ことはない reassures that the action is unnecessary; it differs from experiential Vたことがない.
added-n2-24-111|General behavioral norm|人には親切にするものです。|One should be kind to others.|ものだ presents a behavior as a general norm, not just a description of one person's action.
added-n2-24-111|Normative prohibition|人の失敗を笑うものではありません。|One should not laugh at other people's mistakes.|ものではない states that the behavior is not appropriate as a norm.

added-n2-24-111|Negative intention versus forceful rejection|もう負けるまいと思った。こんなことで諦めるものか。|I resolved not to lose again. There is no way I will give up over this.|まい states negative intention; ものか adds an emphatic emotional rejection.

skm2-c25-zu-niwa-irarenai|Uncontrollable impulse|その話を聞くと、笑わずにはいられません。|When I hear that story, I cannot help laughing.|The impulse makes suppressing the action difficult; it is not an external rule forcing it.

skm2-c25-zu-niwa-irarenai|Irregular する|困っている人を見ると、何かしないではいられません。|When I see someone in trouble, I cannot help doing something.|ないではいられない is the ordinary negative-form alternative. The ず variant of する is せずにはいられない.

skm2-c24-zaru-wo-enai|Circumstances leave no alternative|台風のため、旅行を中止せざるを得ませんでした。|Because of the typhoon, we had no choice but to cancel the trip.|する changes to せざる; the compulsion comes from circumstances rather than an irresistible emotion.

skm2-c24-zaru-wo-enai|Forced decision despite preference|費用が高すぎるので、計画を見直さざるを得ません。|The cost is too high, so we have no choice but to revise the plan.|The expression presents a decision as unavoidable, often contrary to the preferred course.
skm2-c25-te-tamaranai|Physical sensation|暑くてたまりません。|It is unbearably hot.|い-adjectiveくて attaches before たまらない to express an intense sensation.
skm2-c25-te-tamaranai|Strong positive feeling|旅行が楽しみでしかたがありません。|I am tremendously excited about the trip.|な-adjectiveで precedes the expression; strong intensity need not be negative or painful.

added-n2-25-112|Spontaneously arising concern|家族のことが心配でなりません。|I cannot stop worrying about my family.|て/でならない commonly expresses a feeling or thought arising insistently, rather than an external prohibition.
added-n2-25-112|Unavoidable obligation|約束したので、行かないわけにはいきません。|Since I promised, I have to go.|The double negative says that refraining from the action is unacceptable; it does not mean I cannot go.
added-n2-26-113|Longstanding wish|いつかこの町に住んでみたいものです。|I would love to live in this town someday.|たいものだ adds a reflective or strong wish, rather than merely announcing an immediate plan.
added-n2-26-113|Desired action by someone else|もう少し静かにしてほしいものです。|I really wish they would be a little quieter.|てほしいものだ expresses a strong wish about another person's behavior and can sound critical.

added-n2-26-113|Search for a way to achieve a wish|もっと簡単にできないものでしょうか。|Could there be a simpler way to do it?|ないものか searches for a hoped-for possibility; it is not an ordinary factual negative question.
added-n2-26-114|Recollection|学生のころは、よく夜遅くまで話したものです。|When we were students, we often talked until late at night.|Vたものだ recalls a repeated past experience.

added-n2-26-114|An affecting quality|彼女の話には、人を元気にするものがあります。|There is something in her story that cheers people up.|ものがある identifies a quality that makes an impression; it does not refer to a concrete object hidden in the story.
added-n2-26-114|Exclamation|あのとき、どれほど心配したことか。|How worried I was at that time!|ことか is exclamatory after a degree expression, not a request for a numerical answer.

added-n2-26-114|Exclamation of deep feeling|遠いところをわざわざお越しいただき、本当にありがたいことです。|To have you come all this way from afar, how truly thankful I am!|Adjective + ことだ expresses deep, sincere personal emotion or exclamation, distinct from the practical advice pattern V-ことだ.
added-n2-a-116|Formal domain or sphere|現代社会において、情報セキュリティの確保は極めて重要である。|In modern society, ensuring information security is extremely important.|Noun + において marks formal sphere, domain, or era.

added-n2-a-116|Attributive modifying a noun|国際会議における合意に基づき、新たな規制が導入された。|Based on the agreement at the international conference, new regulations were introduced.|Noun + における + Noun acts as an attributive modifier for formal location or occasion.

added-n2-a-116|Preparations prior to an event|新工場の稼働に先立ち、近隣住民への説明会を開いた。|Prior to commencing operations at the new factory, an explanatory meeting for local residents was held.|Noun + に先立ち / に先立って describes deliberate preparatory actions before a major milestone.

added-n2-b-117|Concession acknowledging a label|まだ春浅いとはいいながら、日差しには温もりが感じられる。|Although it is still early spring, warmth can be felt in the sunlight.|とはいいながら concedes a named condition while qualifying what actually holds.

added-n2-b-117|Judging from a standpoint|実用性の面からいうと、こちらのデザインのほうが優れている。|From the standpoint of practicality, this design is superior.|からいうと / からすると specifies the criterion or perspective adopted for evaluation.

added-n2-c-118|Archaic negative in fixed idiom (ざる)|これだけの証拠を突きつけられては、事実を認めざるを得ない。|Confronted with this much evidence, I have no choice but to admit the truth.|ざる survives in the modern construction ざるを得ない.
added-n2-c-118|Negative determination (まい)|二度とあのような愚かな過ちは繰り返すまいと心に誓った。|I vowed in my heart never to repeat such a foolish mistake.|V-辞書形 + まい expresses strong negative intention ('will not').
added-n2-c-118|Negative conjecture (まい)|この空模様では、今夜の雨は降るまい。|Given this weather, it probably will not rain tonight.|V-辞書形 + まい expresses negative conjecture ('probably will not').
added-n2-c-118|Concessive contrast (つつも)|将来の進路について悩みつつも、日々の勉強を続けている。|While agonizing over my future course, I continue my daily studies.|V-stem + つつも expresses concession ('although / while').

added-n2-c-118|Formal simultaneous action (つつ)|資料に目を通しつつ、会議の開始を待った。|While glancing through the documents, I waited for the meeting to start.|V-stem + つつ expresses formal simultaneous action equivalent to ながら.

added-n2-c-118|Concession with せよ (にせよ)|理由の如何にせよ、無断欠席は認められない。|Whatever the reason may be, unexcused absence cannot be permitted.|にせよ derives from the imperative せよ and means 'even granting / regardless of'.
added-n2-c-118|Formal duty with べき (べし)|できる限りの準備は今するべきだ。|We ought to make whatever preparations we can right now.|べき derives from classical べし and expresses moral duty or logical necessity.

added-n2-d-119|Qualified admission with reservation|この本は読んだことは読んだが、内容があまり理解できなかった。|I did indeed read this book, but I could not understand much of the content.|V-たことはV-たが concedes the action occurred before stating a reservation.

added-n2-d-119|Speaker's emotional evaluation|嬉しいことに、第一志望の大学から合格通知が届いた。|Delightfully, an acceptance letter arrived from my top-choice university.|Adjective/V-た + ことに introduces the speaker's emotional reaction to the reported fact.

added-n2-d-120|Drawing an interpretation of circumstances|連絡がないということは、今回の交渉は不成立に終わったということだ。|The fact that there is no contact means that this negotiation ended without an agreement.|AということはBということだ draws a logical interpretation of what a situation signifies.

added-n2-d-120|Formal relay of news or reports|天気予報によると、午後から沿岸部で強い雨が降るということです。|According to the weather forecast, heavy rain will reportedly fall in coastal areas from this afternoon.|Clause + ということです formally relays reported information or official forecasts.

added-n2-e-121|Natural logical conclusion|夜通し起きて作業をしていたのか。道理で眠そうな顔をしているわけだ。|You were up working all night? No wonder you look so sleepy.|わけだ concludes that an observed state is entirely natural given the discovered explanation.

added-n2-e-121|Origin of a name or judgment|富士山がよく見えるところから、この坂は「富士見坂」と名付けられた。|Because Mount Fuji is clearly visible from here, this slope was named Fujimizaka.|ところから identifies an observable physical origin or trigger for a name.

added-n2-f-122|Informal listing of complaints|彼は忙しいだの疲れただのと文句ばかり言って、少しも手伝おうとしない。|He keeps complaining that he is busy or tired, and makes no effort to help.|AだのBだの lists examples with an informal, often critical tone.

added-n2-f-122|Formal exclusive restriction|当施設の利用は登録会員のみに限定されており、一般の入場はできません。|Use of this facility is strictly limited to registered members only; general admission is not permitted.|Noun + のみ formally restricts scope to 'only' without additive nuance.

added-n2-g-123|Sudden occurrence outside speaker's will|疲れてベッドに横になったとたんに、あっという間に眠りに落ちた。|The moment I lay down on the bed from exhaustion, I fell fast asleep in an instant.|たとたん typically pairs with an immediate, non-volitional event in clause two.

added-n2-g-123|First-person visceral sensation|一人で遠い国に暮らしていると、家族の声が無性に聞きたくてたまらない。|Living alone in a distant country, I am dying to hear my family's voices.|〜てたまらない expresses uncontrollable first-person sensations or desires.

added-n2-p2-1-128|Correlative negative conditional|必要な書類を揃えないことには、申請を受け付けることはできません。|Unless you gather all the required documents, we cannot accept your application.|〜ないことには pairs with a negative result clause 〜ない.

added-n2-p2-1-128|Spanning temporal range|今夜から明日の明け方にかけて、激しい雷雨になる見込みです。|From tonight through tomorrow dawn, severe thunderstorms are expected.|〜から〜にかけて pairs starting boundary and ending approximate horizon.

added-n2-p2-2-129|Attributive modifying an abstract noun|国民の信頼に応える政治を行うことが、今最も求められている。|Conducting politics that responds to the trust of the citizens is what is most demanded now.|〜に応える directly modifies the abstract noun 政治 within the subject clause.

added-n2-p2-2-129|Noun modification with contextual preposition|環境問題に関する国際的な関心は、年々高まりを見せている。|International interest concerning environmental issues is showing an increase year by year.|〜に関する attaches to Noun to modify the following noun phrase 関心.

added-n2-p2-3-130|Partial negation with modal hedge|この提案に賛成できないわけではないが、予算の配分には再考の余地がある。|It is not that I cannot agree to this proposal, but there is room to reconsider the budget allocation.|わけではない restricts negation so that the proposition is not categorically denied.

added-n2-p2-3-130|Double negative expressing possibility|彼ほどの能力があれば、この難問を解決できないこともないだろう。|With abilities like his, it is not impossible that he could solve this difficult problem.|〜ないこともない uses double negation to assert a modest possibility.

added-n2-p3-1-141|Opening and closing modal correlation|たとえ困難な道であっても、最後まで全力を尽くすつもりです。|Even if it is a difficult road, I intend to give it my all until the very end.|Opening たとえ correlates with closing volitional/commitment expression.

added-n2-p3-1-141|Conjecture frame across the sentence|もし彼が関与していたとしたら、事態は極めて深刻だと言わざるを得ない。|If he were indeed involved, we would have no choice but to say the situation is extremely serious.|Opening もし〜としたら correlates with closing evaluative conclusion.

added-n2-p3-2-142|Tense contrast in temporal clause|食事をする前に手を洗い、食事が終わった後で薬を飲んだ。|I washed my hands before eating, and took my medicine after the meal finished.|Tense before 前 is non-past (する); tense after 終わった reflects completed sequence.

added-n2-p3-2-142|Relative tense in descriptive narration|昨日見た映画は、昔読んだ小説を映画化したものだった。|The movie I watched yesterday was an adaptation of a novel I had read long ago.|Relative past tenses (見た、読んだ) maintain coherent retrospective framing.

added-n2-p3-3-143|Natural automatic outcome with と|春になると、公園の桜が一斉に咲き乱れる。|When spring arrives, cherry blossoms in the park burst into bloom all at once.|Conditional と marks invariant seasonal consequence without speaker volition in the clause.

added-n2-p3-3-143|Subjective recommendation with たら|分からないことがあれば、遠慮せずにいつでも質問してください。|If there is anything you do not understand, please ask anytime without hesitation.|Conditional たら smoothly accommodates advice and polite directives.

added-n2-p3-4-144|Intransitive natural occurrence|強い風でドアが閉まり、室内の書類が散らかった。|The door shut in the strong wind, and documents in the room got scattered.|Intransitive 閉まる focuses on the spontaneous event rather than an intentional actor.

added-n2-p3-4-144|Transitive deliberate intervention|冷気が入らないように、窓をしっかり閉めておいた。|So that cold air would not enter, I shut the window firmly in advance.|Transitive 閉める focuses on purposeful human intervention.

added-n2-p3-5-145|Development reaching the present with てくる|これまで多くの困難を乗り越えてきた。|We have overcome many hardships up to this point.|〜てくる traces progressive development from the past approaching the current moment.

added-n2-p3-5-145|Evolution heading into the future with ていく|この技術は今後さらに発展していくだろう。|This technology will likely continue to develop further into the future.|〜ていく projects continuous development moving forward from the present.

added-n2-p3-6-146|Adversity passive with indirect victim|満員電車で隣の人に足を踏まれて痛かった。|I had my foot stepped on by the person next to me on the crowded train, and it hurt.|Indirect adversity passive marks the affected person as subject and actor with に.

added-n2-p3-6-146|Causative permission|親は子供に好きな習い事を自由にやらせてくれた。|The parents generously let their child freely pursue whatever extracurricular lessons they wanted.|Causative with てくれる expresses gracious permission granted to an actor.

skm2-c26-te-itadaku|Humble receipt of corporate favor|お忙しいところ恐縮ですが、企画書をご確認いただけますでしょうか。|I apologize for troubling you when busy, but could you kindly review the proposal?|Verb-て + いただく politely solicits a superior's or client's favorable action.

skm2-c26-te-itadaku|Gracious action performed by superior|社長自ら私たちの研究室まで足を運んでくださった。|The company president graciously took the trouble to visit our laboratory in person.|Verb-て + くださる honors an action performed by an esteemed superior for our group.
added-n2-p3-7-147|In-group benefactive direction|友人が困っていたので、私のノートを貸してあげた。|Because my friend was having trouble, I lent them my notebook.|〜てあげる indicates doing a favor outwards for a peer.

added-n2-p3-7-147|Received kindness from another|先輩が仕事の進め方を丁寧に教えてくれた。|My senior colleague kindly taught me how to proceed with the work.|〜てくれる marks an action performed by another for the benefit of the speaker.

added-n2-p3-8-148|Textual reference summarizing previous statement|若者の読書離れが進んでいる。この問題には早急な対策が必要だ。|Young people reading fewer books is progressing. Urgent countermeasures are required for this problem.|Demonstrative この summarizes the previously introduced socioeconomic phenomenon.

added-n2-p3-8-148|Shared psychological knowledge with あ|あのときの苦しい経験があったからこそ、今の成功がある。|It is precisely because of that painful experience back then that we have today's success.|Demonstrative あの recalls an experience vividly shared in psychological memory.
added-n2-p3-9-149|Topic vs contrastive は|兄は外で遊ぶのが好きだが、弟は家で読書をするのが好きだ。|My older brother likes playing outside, but my younger brother likes reading at home.|は marks contrast between parallel topics.

added-n2-p3-9-149|Neutral description with が|外で激しい雨が降り始めたので、窓を閉めた。|Because heavy rain began falling outside, I shut the window.|が in subordinate clauses neutrally marks the subject of natural phenomena.

added-n2-p3-10-150|Adversative qualification with ただし|全品半額セールを実施します。ただし、一部の限定品は対象外です。|We are conducting a half-price sale on all items. However, select limited-edition goods are excluded.|ただし adds a limiting condition or proviso to the preceding general statement.

added-n2-p3-10-150|Consequential development with したがって|原材料費が高騰している。したがって、製品価格を改定せざるを得ない。|Raw material costs are soaring. Consequently, we are compelled to revise product prices.|したがって introduces a formal logical consequence in business writing.

added-n2-p3-10-150|Cumulative addition with しかも|このアパートは駅に近くて便利だ。しかも、家賃が周辺の相場より安い。|This apartment is close to the station and convenient. Moreover, the rent is cheaper than the surrounding market rate.|しかも adds another supportive point of the same evaluation or greater intensity.

added-n2-p3-10-150|Adversative persistence with それでも|宝くじが当たる確率は極めて低い。それでも、人々は夢を求めて買い続ける。|The probability of winning the lottery is extremely low. Even so, people keep buying tickets pursuing the dream.|それでも indicates that the subsequent fact or action persists despite the preceding reality.

added-n2-p3-10-150|Clarification and reformulation with すなわち|母の兄、すなわち私のおじが来週遊びに来ます。|My mother's elder brother, that is to say my uncle, is coming to visit next week.|すなわち restates or clarifies the preceding term in other words.

added-n2-p3-11-151|Reformulation with つまり|彼は一言も返事をしなかった。つまり、納得していないということだ。|He did not utter a single reply. In other words, he does not agree.|つまり restates the essential meaning of an observation in clearer terms.

added-n2-p3-11-151|Syntactic omission in cohesive text|田中さんは資料を手に取り、しばらく黙って（資料を）眺めていた。|Tanaka picked up the document and gazed at it silently for a while.|Cohesive prose omits previously mentioned direct objects to avoid cumbersome repetition.

added-n2-p3-12-152|Academic expository style|本研究の目的は、日本語の文法構造を解明することにある。|The objective of this research consists in elucidating Japanese grammatical structures.|Expository academic writing consistently maintains だ/である forms.

added-n2-p3-12-152|Polite correspondence style|ご不明な点がございましたら、いつでも担当者までご連絡ください。|Should you have any unclear points, please contact the person in charge at any time.|Polite business correspondence maintains consistent です/ます honorific harmony.

skm2-c25-te-wa-irarenai|Situational urgency|もうすぐ試験が始まるから、いつまでものんびりしてはいられない。|The exam will begin soon, so I cannot afford to be idling around forever.|Time pressure prevents continuing in a relaxed state.

skm2-c25-te-wa-irarenai|Maturity and self-reliance|社会人になったのだから、親に甘えてばかりはいられない。|Now that I am a working adult, I can't keep depending on my parents.|Growing up means one cannot continue childhood dependence.

skm2-c10-nuki-de|Without standard ingredient or feature|朝は時間がなかったので、朝食抜きで会社へ向かった。|Because I had no time in the morning, I headed to the office without breakfast.|Noun + 抜きで indicates doing an action while omitting a regular accompanying item.

skm2-c10-nuki-de|Excluding someone's presence|彼の協力抜きには、この大規模なイベントの成功はあり得なかった。|Without his cooperation, the success of this large-scale event could never have occurred.|〜抜きには…ない asserts that an outcome would be impossible without the named element.

skm2-c14-ippou-de|Coexisting contrasting developments|都市部で地価が上昇する一方で、過疎地では空き家が増え続けている。|While land prices rise in urban areas, vacant houses continue to multiply in depopulated regions.|Clause + 一方で juxtaposes two simultaneous trends.

skm2-c14-ippou-de|Dual personal characteristics|彼は仕事に対して非常に厳しい一方で、部下の私生活には深い思いやりを見せる。|While he is extremely strict about work, he shows deep consideration for his subordinates' personal lives.|Coexisting facets of a single person's personality.

skm2-c17-wo-keiki-ni|Catalyst for personal reform|海外赴任を契機として、本格的に英会話の勉強を始めた。|Taking his overseas assignment as a catalyst, he began studying English conversation in earnest.|〜を契機として marks a decisive life event sparking systematic personal change.

skm2-c17-wo-keiki-ni|Historical turning point|市民革命を契機に、国の政治体制は大きく近代化へと舵を切った。|Taking the civic revolution as a turning point, the nation's political system steered heavily toward modernization.|Historical turning point sparking societal transformation.

skm2-c18-kara-koso|Tough love and honest advice|あなたの将来を心から案じているからこそ、苦言を呈しているのです。|It is precisely because I care about your future from the bottom of my heart that I offer harsh advice.|からこそ singles out the genuine core reason, rejecting other motivations.

skm2-c18-kara-koso|Overcoming hardship|苦しい練習を耐え抜いたからこそ、優勝した瞬間の感動はひとしおだった。|It was precisely because we endured grueling practice that the emotion of victory was so intense.|Singular justification explaining the magnitude of reward.

skm2-p2-kko-nai|Adamant denial of possibility|あんなに頑固な部長が、私たちの要求を簡単に受け入れっこないよ。|There is no way in hell such a stubborn manager would easily accept our demands.|Colloquial categorical rejection of an improbable premise.

skm2-p2-kko-nai|Challenging unrealistic workload|たった二日間でこの分厚い報告書を全部翻訳できっこない。|There is no way anyone could translate this entire thick report in just two days.|Verb-stem + っこない emphasizes absolute practical impossibility.

gp-kato-omou-to|Sudden weather shift|青空が広がっていたかと思うと、急に大粒の雨が降り出してきた。|No sooner had blue skies spread than large raindrops suddenly began pouring down.|Instantaneous unexpected shift in natural phenomena.

gp-kato-omou-to|Rapid change in state|泣いていた赤ちゃんが、お母さんの顔を見たかと思うと、にこっと笑った。|The crying baby, no sooner had it seen its mother's face, broke into a bright smile.|Instantaneous emotional turnaround upon perception.

gp-kanai-ka|Instantaneous subsequent action|授業終了のチャイムが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。|Barely had the class-end chime sounded when the students bolted out of the classroom.|V-るかV-ないかのうちに captures overlapping immediacy before an action even fully ends.
gp-kanai-ka|Urgent departure|夜が明けるか明けないかのうちに、登山隊は山頂を目指して出発した。|Before dawn had even fully broken, the mountaineering expedition set out for the summit.|Immediacy at the very threshold of an event.

gp-shidai|Business commitment upon condition|日程が確定し次第、改めてメールにてご連絡申し上げます。|As soon as the schedule is confirmed, I will contact you again by email.|Verb-stem + 次第 promises resolute subsequent action immediately upon prerequisite completion.
gp-shidai|Readiness for action|準備が整い次第、直ちに作業を再開してください。|As soon as preparations are in order, please resume operations immediately.|Directive conditioned on prompt prerequisite fulfillment.

gp-amari|Extreme sorrow resulting in illness|最愛のペットを失った悲しみのあまり、彼女は数日間寝込んでしまった。|From the sheer excess of sorrow over losing her beloved pet, she stayed bedridden for several days.|Noun + のあまり describes severe physical or mental reaction from overwhelming grief.

gp-amari|Excessive haste leading to mistake|先を急いだあまり、曲がるべき交差点を通り過ぎてしまった。|From hurrying too much, I drove right past the intersection where I should have turned.|V-た + あまり indicates an inadvertent error caused by overdoing an action.

gp-ageku|Exhausting dispute ending in severance|何時間も激しく口論したあげく、二人は絶交してしまった。|After arguing fiercely for hours on end, the two ended up completely breaking off their friendship.|V-た + あげく(に) emphasizes that prolonged agonizing friction culminated in a regrettable outcome.

gp-ageku|Indecision ending in lost chance|あれこれ迷ったあげくに、結局どの物件も契約できずに終わった。|After agonizing endlessly back and forth, I ended up unable to sign a lease for any property.|Prolonged indecision culminating in total futility.

gp-mononara|Unrealizable wish|やり直せるものなら、人生をもう一度最初からやり直したい。|If it were possible to start over, I would want to redo life once more from the very beginning.|Potential + ものなら assumes an impossible condition to express profound longing.

gp-mononara|Warning against reckless action|そんな失礼な口を利こうものなら、ただでは済まないぞ。|If you should dare speak so rudely, you won't get away with it!|Volitional + ものなら frames a dangerous trigger that would invite terrible retribution.

gp-naikotoniwa|Prerequisite for contract|双方の合意が得られないことには、契約を締結することはできません。|Unless mutual agreement is obtained from both sides, we cannot conclude the contract.|〜ないことには sets an indispensable condition for contract execution.

gp-naikotoniwa|Prerequisite for decision|現地の被害状況を直接確認しないことには、支援の規模を判断できない。|Unless we inspect the local damage directly, we cannot judge the scale of required relief.|Direct inspection is an essential prerequisite for making a decision.

gp-ni-kagiri|Privilege restricted to specific group|本日ご来場のお客様に限り、特製記念品を差し上げます。|Strictly limited to guests attending today, we present a special commemorative gift.|Noun + に限り formally announces an exclusive privilege.

gp-ni-kagiri|First-time customer offer|初回注文の方に限り、配送料を無料とさせていただきます。|Limited exclusively to first-time orders, we offer free shipping.|Commercial privilege strictly confined to eligible first-time patrons.
gp-ni-kagitte|Unlucky coincidence|傘を持っていない日に限って、突然大雨が降ってくる。|Of all days, on the very day I don't have an umbrella, sudden heavy rain pours down.|〜に限って laments an ironic, unlucky coincidence.

gp-ni-kagitte|Selective trust contradicted|普段は時間に正確な山田さんに限って、無断で遅刻するはずがない。|Yamada-san of all people, who is normally so punctual, would surely never be late without notice.|Singling out a trusted individual as an exception to negative assumptions.

gp-bakarika|Astonishing addition beyond expectation|彼は英語ばかりか、フランス語やロシア語まで流暢に話す。|Not only English, he even speaks French and Russian with fluency.|Noun + ばかりか escalates beyond a baseline expectation to an even more impressive degree.
gp-bakarika|Compounded adversity|雨が激しくなったばかりか、強い風まで吹き荒れてきた。|Not only did the rain intensify, but fierce winds came howling in as well.|Compounding adverse conditions extending to a worse degree.

gp-monono|Fact admitted but falling short|新しいパソコンを購入したものの、機能が多すぎて使いこなせない。|Although I bought a new computer, there are too many features and I cannot master them.|Conceding an action occurred while contrasting it with an unsatisfactory outcome.

gp-monono|Calendar status vs actual reality|暦の上では立春とはいうものの、まだまだ厳しい寒さが続いている。|Although on the calendar it is the onset of spring, severe cold is still continuing.|とはいうものの acknowledges a nominal label while stating the contradictory physical reality.

gp-dokoroka|Far from good, actually far worse|病状は回復するどころか、ますます悪化の一途をたどっている。|Far from recovering, the patient's condition is worsening further by the day.|どころか emphatically negates a favorable expectation in favor of a far worse reality.

gp-dokoroka|Inability to do even the basic minimum|忙しくて海外旅行どころか、近くの温泉に一泊することさえできない。|I am so busy that far from an overseas trip, I cannot even stay a single night at a nearby hot spring.|Negating a grand plan to emphasize that even modest recreation is impossible.

gp-ni-hokaranaranai|Absolute conviction of sole reason|今回のプロジェクトの成功は、チーム全員の献身的な努力の賜物にほかならない。|The success of this project is nothing other than the fruit of dedicated effort by the entire team.|Formal emphatic assertion identifying the single true cause.

gp-ni-hokaranaranai|Sole motivation for honesty|私が厳しく指導するのは、君の成長を心から願っているからにほかならない。|My instructing you strictly is none other than because I truly desire your growth.|からにほかならない asserts with total conviction the sole benevolent motivation.
gp-kkonai-kanenai|Impossibility with っこない|素人の私がプロの囲碁棋士に勝ちっこない。|There is no way a complete amateur like me could defeat a professional Go player.|Verb-stem + っこない emphatically denies any possibility.

gp-kkonai-kanenai|Severe risk with かねない|あんな乱暴な運転を続けていたら、大事故を起こしかねない。|If he continues driving so recklessly, he is liable to cause a major accident.|Verb-stem + かねない warns of dangerous potential catastrophe.

gp-zaruwokenai|Unwilling resignation to harsh reality|不採算事業の継続は困難であり、事業の縮小を決断せざるを得ない。|Continuing unprofitable business operations is difficult, so management is compelled to decide on downsizing.|せざるを得ない expresses reluctant administrative compulsion against one's wishes.

gp-zaruwokenai|Conceding error in light of evidence|これだけ決定的な証拠を見せられては、自分の非を認めざるを得ない。|Presented with such decisive evidence, I am compelled to admit my fault.|Objective reality leaving zero alternative but to concede.

gp-ni-tsurete|Proportional natural change|標高が高くなるにつれて、気温が次第に下がってくる。|As altitude increases, the temperature gradually drops.|〜につれて describes natural proportional correlation between two progressing variables.

gp-ni-tsurete|Societal evolution over time|時代の変化につれて、人々の価値観や生活様式も多様化してきた。|As the times change, people's values and lifestyles have also diversified.|Proportional evolution in social values accompanying the passage of time.

gp-ni-oujite|Customized to individual requirements|生徒一人ひとりの理解度に応じて、教える内容や進度を調整する。|According to each student's level of comprehension, we adjust the teaching content and pacing.|〜に応じて modulates instruction in tailored proportion to recipient capacity.

gp-ni-oujite|Flexible scaling by budget|ご予算に応じて、最適な旅行プランをいくつかご提案いたします。|In accordance with your budget, we will propose several optimal travel plans.|Modulating commercial options scaled to client financial parameters.

gp-to-ittara|Astonishing degree of sensation|冬の朝の寒さといったら、布団から出るのが嫌になるほどだ。|The cold of a winter morning is so intense that you dread coming out of the futon!|〜といったら highlights an astonishing or extreme degree of feeling.

gp-to-ittara|Astonishing degree of beauty|山頂から見渡した夜景の美しさといったら、言葉を失うほどだった。|The breathtaking beauty of the night view from the summit was such that it left me speechless!|Exclamatory emphasis on an extraordinary visual experience.

gp-wo-towazu|Open to all without distinction|このボランティア活動は、年齢や国籍を問わずどなたでも参加できます。|This volunteer activity is open to anyone regardless of age or nationality.|Noun + を問わず indicates universal openness without condition or exclusion.

gp-wo-towazu|Available at all times|当ホテルのフィットネスジムは、昼夜を問わず24時間いつでもご利用いただけます。|Our hotel fitness gym can be used 24 hours a day, regardless of whether it is day or night.|Removing temporal restrictions to announce all-hours availability.

gp-ha-tomokaku|Setting aside secondary consideration|外見はともかくとして、このアパートは立地と家賃が非常に魅力的だ。|Setting aside its exterior appearance for now, this apartment's location and rent are very attractive.|〜はともかく(として) puts aside a secondary flaw to focus on the decisive priority.

gp-ha-tomokaku|Prioritizing immediate action|勝敗はともかく、選手たちが全力を出し切ることが何よりも大切だ。|Leaving winning or losing aside, what matters above all is that the players give their absolute all.|Setting aside outcome to focus on earnest effort.
